title: One number for spread
question: How do you put a number on how spread out a set of values is?
hook: Two groups can have the exact same average and still be nothing alike.
idea: Variance averages how far values stray from their mean, squared, giving a single number for spread.

beats.prompt: Two classes both average 70 on a test. In class A, everyone scored 70. In class B, half scored 50 and half scored 90. Which class has the larger variance?

choices.label: Class A, since everyone matches the average
choices.feedback: Matching the average means no deviation, which gives zero variance.

choices.label: Class B, since its scores stray far from 70
They tie, since the averages are equal
choices.feedback: Equal averages say nothing about spread, which is what variance measures.

beats.explain: Variance measures how far values are spread from their average, and class B's scores sit well away from 70 while class A's never move.

beats.prompt: Match each term to what it means.
pairs: Expected value of the squared deviation from the mean
The square root of the variance
Computed when all possible observations are present
Computed from only a subset, as an estimate
beats.explain: The definitions link up: variance is the base idea, the standard deviation is its square root, and population versus sample depends on how much data you hold.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: A set of heights is measured in meters.
Variance is the expected value of squared deviations from the mean.
So the variance is measured in the same units as the heights.
The standard deviation, the square root of the variance, is the more commonly reported measure.
beats.explain: Unlike the standard deviation, the variance has units that differ from the variable, which is why the standard deviation is more commonly reported.

beats.prompt: Two measurement errors are uncorrelated. One has variance 4, the other variance 5. What is the variance of their sum?

choices.label: 9, the sum of the two variances
20, the product of the two
choices.feedback: It is tempting to multiply, but variances of uncorrelated variables add.

choices.label: 4.5, the average of the two
choices.feedback: Averaging would shrink the spread, but adding uncorrelated errors makes room for both.

beats.explain: One advantage of variance is that, for uncorrelated random variables, the variance of a sum equals the sum of their variances.
